1.sofaString: 379	Pt, ******, is a 14 y/o female with dilated cardiomyopathy, referred by ***** ******, ****, Transplant Coordinator, for Psychosocial Assessment for Heart Transplant Evaluation.     Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the patient, patient's mother, ********* ********, patient's father, **** ****** , and review of the medical records. Interview with patient's father was completed over the phone. SW spent approximately 75 minutes of face-to-face time with family.     Living situation:  Pt, ******, resides with her mother, and sister in *******, *******. They reside at *** ********** ** *** ***, *******, ** *****. They **** a 3-bedroom apartment. They have one dog, a *********.      Demographics:  Mother:  ********* ********   ***:  **/**/****  Language: English   Education Level: ** ******, CNA and LMT              Employment:  private ********** for Sooth Inc, CNA ** ******* ******** (hasn't started yet)           Phone:  ***-***-****     Father:  **** ******  ***:  **/**/****  Language: French Creole, English  Education Level: High School Diploma       Employment: Unemployed  Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings in Home:  ********- 8     Social History and Support Systems:  ****** lives with her mother, and sister in *******, *******. Mom and dad were never married and separated several years prior. Their current relationship is contentious. Mom moved to ******* with the children in **** ** ****. She states that she chose to move to ******* because she located her brother and he offered for her to **** one of his homes. Other than her brother, the rest of her family resides in *** **** along with the father and his extended family. The parents have a joint custody agreement. The father gets the children for the ****** and ****** holidays. Both parents have parental rights and therefore both parents can consent for treatment. The mother is opposed to having the father consent to any medical treatment without her knowledge. She stated that 'he doesn't understand what is going on and he is just a yes man to you guys.' She was informed that due to their joint custody status, both parents have the ability to consent. SW placed note in patient's chart asking that both parents be informed of and consent to any invasive medical treatment. SW inquired about significant relationships of mom. She reports that her long time significant other is currently incarcerated. She has another as well as friends but reports that she does not allow men in her home because she does not trust them with her children. Of note, she has asked that male nurses not be allowed to care for ****** because it is not proper for men to be touching her daughter. SW reminded her that many of the physicians are male and she stated that they were ok because they were doctors. The father is married to ****** ******, they have been married for two years.   The family's housing situation is tenuous. Mom informed staff that she needed to return home for a meeting to avoid eviction. She has not paid **** for the last several months. This is concerning as this was prior to illness onset and before the mother at the added stressors of this hospital stay.   Mom plans to be the primary caregiver post-transplant. She understands that ****** cannot be left alone for at least the first few months. She plans to have her brother and sister in law assist while she is working. Patient's father reports that he can return to ******* and stay as long as needed to assist with ******'s care.   Mom is currently employed as a private ********** licensed massage therapist with Soothe Inc. She also reports that she recently obtained employment **** ******* ******** as a second job. She will be working ********** as a CNA. She does not receive benefits through her work with Soothe Inc. She has not yet started her job ** ******* ******** and therefore ineligible for benefits.  The father is unemployed and does not pay child support.   ****** is finishing up the 9th grade at **** *** **** School. She missed the end of the school year due to illness. ****** reports to enjoy going to the mall, out to eat, and spending time with friends. SW discussed the possibility of beginning next year in hospital homebound if needed. Mom denies any history of developmental or educational delays.   Mom and dad both report to identify as *********. They both deny any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc. When asked if she had an exception to receiving a heart transplant she did not initially give a direct answer. She first stated that where she is from (*******), they do not do transplants. They just let nature take its course. She went on to say that if ******'s heart stopped working she would be agreeable to transplant if it was her only option. SW attempted to further educate and explore but patient's mother did not give any further information. During this conversation patient's mother ******* ******'s current condition to an aunt who needed a stent placed and then got better. Patient's father stated that he is agreeable to whatever the medical team thinks is needed. SW inquired what he would do if he and patient's mother ********* on medical plan and he responded 'I will agree with the medical team'. Patient's father also seems to have poor insight and understanding of patient's medical condition. [SM1]    Course of illness:     ****** is a 14 y/o female who is admitted for evaluation of dilated cardiomyopathy. Mom reports that she initially became sick approximately 1 week prior to initial hospitalization after eating *********. Mom informed SW that she believes that ****** ate contaminated food at ********* and that is why she is now sick. During the 1 week of being ill, mom believed it to be a stomach virus. When she did not improve, mom had her evaluated at *** ******* ******** **. **** did an EKG at this time and sent her home from the ER. Mom reports that over the next few days they went to the beach and school. When she was at school, she began feeling ill again and had mom pick her up from school. Around this time, mom also received a call from the cardiologist wanting to schedule an appointment. Mom was unsure why she was receiving this call for an appointment and wanted a second opinion. She then decided to take ****** to St ******'s Hospital ER. Once there, she was admitted, started on IV medications and transfer to ** ****** ****** was initiated.   This history varies a little from the history given in the medical records. It states that she was in her usual state of health until 1 week ago when without an inciting factor, she started having diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea. Throughout the week, she noticed she was having tachycardia which prompted them to go to ******* ******** ******** where after hydration and an EKG, she was sent home. The next day, mom received a call from Dr. ****** (cardiologist) prompting them to go to the ED at St. ******'s because her EKG was abnormal and was concerning for LV hypertrophy.     Financial situation:  The family relies on the earned income of from the mother's jobs. The family's income does not meet their needs each month. The father does not assist financially. They are in the process of a possible eviction as mom has been unable to pay **** for the last several months. There will also be a significant loss of income if patient's mother is unable to work post-transplant. SW discussed fundraising but she was not open to the idea. SW has also placed a social security disability referral. When asked what mom plans to do to assist with the loss of income, she stated that she would have to go on government assistance. SW discussed the possibility of **** funds but also tried to encourage other ideas for financial planning.   Upon admission, ****** was uninsured. Mom reports that she usually insures that the children are on insurance through her employment or through Medicaid. It was unclear why this current Medicaid ***** of **** had lapsed. It is now active again and her SOC amount is $2014. SW discussed this with mom. She would benefit from having either full Medicaid, insurance through mother's employment, or possibly a plan through the healthcare marketplace. SW has applied for disability and if approved, hopefully ****** will also be approved for full Medicaid.   Mom has one vehicle and reports that transportation will not be a barrier.      Family History:  Mom denies any current mental health, criminal, drug, or DCF history.    Mom does endorse history of DCF involvement with herself as a child. She was placed in ****** care due to family's inability to care for her.      Adherence:  There are concerns for adherence with this family. The patient's mother refused a heart catheterization on **/**. The family was initially told that the insert site would be the groin. When they spoke with the physician completing the cath the morning of **/** it was explained that they would be going in through the neck. Mom informed that the medical team is 'lying' to her. She then proceeded to graphically explain the risks of the procedure (blood ******** out of the neck, bleeding out, stroke, etc.) in front of the ******. She stated that she has done her research and going through the 'carotid artery' was too high risk and she would not consent for that. She stated that she is the mother and she gets to decide which way it is done, and she wants it done through the groin. Several physicians spoke to patient's mother and informed that the carotid artery is not used and that going through the neck would be easier on the ******. Mom still refused unless it could be guaranteed that they would enter through the groin.   Mom and ****** disclosed that she does not take pills. She will do liquids or chewables but cannot swallow pills. SW discussed the importance of being able to take pill form medication, especially due to her age and possible transplant. They confirmed understanding and said they were willing to work on this.   SW called and spoke with the SW at ** ******'s regarding compliance, and reported prior treatment ********.  She informed SW that the only thing she was aware of was that mom refused transfer when airlift team came overnight to transfer to ******. She agreed to transfer after speaking with Cardiologist the next day.      Assessment and recommendations:   SW has significant concerns about proceeding with transplant with this family. Both the mother and the father have a poor understanding of patient's medical condition. Patient's mother initially refused the cath informing physicians that she 'is the mother and gets to tell the doctor how they get to do the cath'. The family has very low resources and their income does not meet their needs each month, even prior to illness and hospitalization. The mother has already been served with an eviction notice. She is attempting to catch up on the **** but is unsure that she will be able to. The father does not help out financially. The family has very limited support, the only person that patient's mother could identify as support is her brother and sister in law. Since hospitalization, they have not been to see ******, and it is unsure whether they will actually participate and assist this family. Patient's father verbally informed SW that he can be here for as long as needed but left the hospital Friday to return to *** **** without informing medical team or leaving a contact phone number. To this SW's knowledge, he has not called to speak with medical team for updates since leaving. He is unemployed, so SW unsure how he will financially manage the travel or staying long term in Gainesville.   SW met with ****** alone to assess her feelings towards transplant. ******'s presented with flat affect and was difficult to engage. She does not like being in the hospital and a prolonged could likely be detrimental to her mental health. SW inquired about her understanding current condition and of transplant. She was unable to describe her current health condition. She stated that transplant is a surgery and that she will get a new heart. She endorsed feeling fearful about transplant. She informed SW that she does not want transplant. SW attempted to discuss further, including the risks if she refuses treatment but ****** would not engage further in conversation. SW offered to have physician and child life meet with her to explain more but she declined. She stated that she does not like discussing it and does not want any information.   It would be a very high risk to proceed with transplant with this family due to the numerous psychosocial concerns.       IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  4     Family Background & Social Support -  4     Financial/Insurance - 4     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 3     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  2     Adherence -4     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process - 4     Health Literacy -  3     Coping Skills - 4     Total:  32 High-Severe Risk     The family scores as high-severe risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.          Recommendations:  *Provide continuing education to the patient and family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  *Arrange for ********* to work with ****** regarding transplant education.  *Ongoing involvement of psychology- arrange outpatient therapy.  *Assist family with developing financial plan.  *Offer support and guidance to family as needed.     ******** *****, LCSW  Pediatric Heart and Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****[SM1]literacy
